narrative.intro: Thalle Construction obligated $1.9B in federal contract funds in FY2026 to date. Thalle Construction received 3 awards this fiscal year, with an average award size of $639M, and obligations are up 571.1% year over year. Historical obligations show uneven activity: FY21 was $167M, FY22 was $213M, FY23 was $16.1M, FY24 was $366M, and FY25 was $285M. The Department of Defense is the dominant buyer, obligating $1.9B. The Department of the Interior is a minor buyer, obligating $114K. Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction is the primary market, accounting for $1.9B in obligations, while Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction accounts for $114K. Current-year totals are partial, representing fiscal year to date obligations rather than a full-year total. This snapshot highlights concentrated DoD business and a reliance on large awards in the current fiscal year.

faq.q: How much does Thalle Construction make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Thalle Construction made $1.9B from federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Current-year totals are partial and reflect fiscal year to date obligations. Historical annual obligations were $167M in FY21, $213M in FY22, $16.1M in FY23, $366M in FY24, and $285M in FY25.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Thalle Construction?
faq.a: The Department of Defense buys most from Thalle Construction, obligating $1.9B. The Department of the Interior also buys from Thalle Construction, obligating $114K.

faq.q: What does Thalle Construction sell to the government?
faq.a: Thalle Construction sells primarily Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction work to the government, accounting for $1.9B in obligations. Thalle Construction also sells Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction work, accounting for $114K in obligations.
